rombik.name: rombik
rombik.tagline: Code → DSTU flowchart: web, API, CLI
rombik.description: A SaaS I designed and run: turns Python, C, C++, C#, Java and Pascal into a clean DSTU 19.701-90 flowchart — the kind colleges still draw by hand for hours. A Go engine (tree-sitter → IR → layout → render), a web editor with pan/zoom and manual lasso-splitting, a public HTTP API, a CLI and a skill for AI agents. Five formats: SVG, PNG, PDF, Typst, Excalidraw. Free PNG, no sign-up.

piton.name: Piton
piton.tagline: A Ukrainian programming language with a homegrown interpreter
piton.description: Lightweight interpreted language with authentic Ukrainian syntax (translit). Recursive descent parser, tree-walking evaluator, Turing-complete. Written from scratch in Go, no yacc/bison. A built-in D2 engine draws SVG flowcharts (DSTU). The interpreter is compiled to WebAssembly via TinyGo — 220 KB, runs directly in the browser without a server.

bench.title: JS vs Go·WASM — same hash, two engines
bench.subtitle: Same SHA-256, same input, two engines. Left: a JS copy of the official Student Hryvnia client. Right: my Go rewrite from SHMiner, compiled to WASM with TinyGo. Lanes run sequentially, 10 seconds each — JS first on a single core, then Go·WASM on N cores. Each lane gets the full CPU to itself, so the numbers stay honest.
bench.speedupBody: that's how much faster Go·WASM is than the official JS miner on your machine — in this configuration
bench.jsModeOriginalHint: verbatim from the official client — with `sleep(1)` every 1000 hashes
bench.disclaimer: Runs on your machine in your browser. The JS lane is single-threaded — a verbatim copy of `calculateBlockHash` from the official client (`await window.crypto.subtle.digest`, optionally + `sleep(1)` every 1000 hashes). The Go·WASM lane spins up a pool of Web Workers — one per core, just like SHMiner's goroutine pool. Difficulty is 20 bits (5 leading zero hex chars), the SHMiner default.
bench.desktopNoteBody: Native Go from the desktop client is much faster than TinyGo·WASM in the browser — native Go's SHA-256 uses SIMD/AVX CPU instructions (4-8 blocks in parallel; scalar WASM does 0), and Web Workers pay for serialization. The real numbers (1000×+ vs the official JS miner) only show up in the actual SHMiner. The Wails app is cross-platform: Linux · macOS · Windows.
